- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk reversal or market panic.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5–7% below peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of smoothing or delay forecast peak by 1–2 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply 2–3 day lag filter to sentiment influence to avoid noise amplification.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast to 3–5 day moving average of sentiment-weighted history.
